sheet: L(θ)=∏f(xᵢ;θ); treat x as fixed and θ as variable.
Solve ℓ′=0 for interior candidates, then check curvature, boundaries and constraints.
MLE invariance: g(θ̂) is an MLE for g(θ) under the usual induced-likelihood convention.
MLE is not guaranteed unbiased or efficient.
Bernoulli(p): p̂=x̄; Poisson(λ): λ̂=x̄; exponential rate λ: λ̂=1/x̄.
Uniform(0,θ): θ̂=x₍ₙ₎; normal variance MLE uses divisor n.
cards: The joint density/probability of observed data viewed as a function of the parameter.
Products become sums and the maximiser is unchanged.
Does every MLE solve the score equation?
Only interior differentiable maxima; boundary cases may not.

scenes.title: Likelihood
scenes.objective: Understand likelihood as a function of parameter for fixed data.
body: Once observations are fixed, their joint density or probability becomes a function of θ: the likelihood. For iid data multiply the individual terms; taking logarithms turns the product into a sum.
Maximising likelihood chooses a parameter value under which the observed sample is most compatible with the model.

items.ask: Write likelihood and log likelihood for iid observations.
Is likelihood a probability distribution over θ?
items.recall: No. It need not integrate to one over parameter values.

scenes.title: Score equation and checks
scenes.objective: Solve score equations and understand limitations.
body: For an interior differentiable maximum, ℓ′(θ)=0. This produces candidates, not a complete solution.
Check second derivative, parameter restrictions and boundaries. Support-dependent models may have a boundary maximum with no score root.

items.why: Interior differentiable maxima satisfy this; boundary maxima may not.

items.claim: Taking log preserves the maximiser of positive likelihood.

scenes.title: Bernoulli MLE
scenes.problem: For iid Bernoulli(p), find the MLE.
scenes.check: Check the endpoints p=0 and p=1 when the sample is all failures or successes.

scenes.title: Poisson MLE
scenes.problem: For iid Poisson(λ), find the MLE.

solution.math: If all observations are zero, the maximiser is λ̂=0.

scenes.title: Exponential rate MLE

solution.math: Rate is inverse-time units; long average waiting time means a small rate.

scenes.check: If the parameter is scale instead, the estimate is x̄.

scenes.title: Invariance
scenes.objective: Transform an MLE to estimate a function of the parameter.
body: When the MLE exists, the standard invariance property gives g(θ̂) as an MLE of g(θ) under the induced-likelihood convention.
For geometric trials-count data E[X]=1/p, so the MLE of the mean is 1/p̂.

items.ask: If p̂ is the MLE and target is 1/p, what candidate follows?

scenes.title: Normal variance MLE
scenes.objective: Distinguish the likelihood estimate from unbiased variance.
scenes.problem: For iid N(μ,σ²), both parameters unknown, state the MLEs.

solution.math: The unbiased estimator uses n−1; the MLE uses n and is biased in finite samples.

scenes.check: Divisor n is the likelihood maximiser.

scenes.title: Uniform(0,θ): boundary maximum
body: The likelihood is θ^(−n) for θ≥x₍ₙ₎ and zero otherwise. It decreases over the feasible region, so the maximum occurs at θ̂=x₍ₙ₎.
This is a parameter-dependent support example: the score −n/θ never vanishes, so the boundary—not the score root—determines the estimate.

items.claim: The MLE of θ in Uniform(0,θ) is x̄.
items.why: The likelihood decreases over its feasible range, maximised at x₍ₙ₎.

items.claim: There is an interior score root.

scenes.title: Geometric distribution and invariance
scenes.problem: For trials-to-first-success geometric pmf p(1−p)^(x−1), find MLE of p and E[X].

scenes.title: Review
body: Likelihood is joint probability/density for observed data viewed as a parameter function. Log likelihood simplifies it.
Score roots are candidates; check curvature, restrictions and boundaries.
Bernoulli/Poisson MLE x̄, exponential rate 1/x̄, Uniform upper endpoint x₍ₙ₎, normal variance divisor n.
MLE is not automatically unbiased or efficient.
